title: HTTP Caching and Cache-Control Headers
objective: Explain how Cache-Control directives (max-age, no-store, private, public) affect browser and shared caches, and identify common caching mistakes.

blocks.title: When caches surprise you
blocks.content: A fix ships to production but users still see the old page. Often the culprit is caching, not your deploy. This lesson focuses on Cache-Control directives and common mistakes.

blocks.title: What Cache-Control does
blocks.content: Cache-Control is an HTTP header that tells browsers and shared caches how responses may be stored and reused. Directives include max-age (freshness lifetime in seconds), no-store (do not store), private (only browser caches), and public (shared caches may store).

blocks.title: Freshness vs revalidation
blocks.content: Within max-age, a cache may reuse a response without contacting the origin. After freshness expires, caches may revalidate. Mixing no-store with max-age is a common misconfiguration — no-store means the response must not be stored in any cache.

blocks.title: Worked examples
blocks.content:
Example 1: Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 — shared caches may serve for one hour.
Example 2: Cache-Control: private, max-age=60 — browser-only, one minute.
Example 3: Cache-Control: no-store — never cache (typical for authenticated HTML).

### Live sandbox outputs (httpbin.org)
- GET: status=200 body='{\n  "args": {},\n  "headers": {\n    "Accept": "*/*",\n    "Accept-Encoding": "gzip'
- POST: status=200 body='{\n  "args": {},\n  "headers": {\n    "Accept": "*/*",\n    "Accept-Encoding": "gzip'
- STATUS_200: status=200 body=''
- STATUS_404: status=404 body=''
- STATUS_500: status=500 body=''

blocks.title: Practical applications
blocks.content:
1) Static assets: long max-age with fingerprinted filenames.
2) Personalized dashboards: private or no-store.
3) CDN misconfig: public caching of Set-Cookie responses — a security/privacy bug.

blocks.title: Hands-on header clinic
blocks.content: Given three response headers, choose the correct directive set and explain who may cache them. Debate edge cases for logged-in users.

blocks.title: Summary
blocks.content: max-age sets freshness; private vs public controls who stores; no-store forbids storage. Validate headers against the sensitivity of the content.

blocks.title: Supplementary videos
blocks.content: Watch an HTTP caching overview focusing on Cache-Control. Suggested: caching section of an HTTP course.

blocks.content: MDN Cache-Control, MDN HTTP caching guide, RFC 9111.

claims.claim_text: no-store means the response must not be stored in any cache.

knowledge_checks.question: What does max-age control?
knowledge_checks.answer: How long a response is considered fresh (in seconds).

knowledge_checks.question: When would you use no-store?
knowledge_checks.answer: When the response must not be stored in any cache (e.g., sensitive pages).

knowledge_checks.question: Difference between private and public?
knowledge_checks.answer: private = browser-only caches; public = shared caches may store.
